open_questions.question: Is day 30 inside the refund window? Are days counted as calendar dates in store local time, or as 24-hour periods from the purchase timestamp?
What does the POS do with a refund after 30 days: block it, allow a manager override, or issue store credit?
Does 'over $500' mean strictly greater than $500.00, so a refund of exactly $500.00 needs no approval?
Is the $500 limit checked against the whole refund transaction, against each tender, or against the running total of all refunds on the same sale?
How does a manager reject an approval at the register, and what happens afterwards: is the refund cancelled, and can it be retried with another manager?
For a partial refund on a split-tender sale, does 'reverse order' mean the last tender is refunded up to its full paid amount before any money goes to the earlier tender?
R4 only limits the total. Can the same line item be refunded a second time if the running total would still be under the original amount?
Does the refund screen let the cashier pick a tender at all, and if so, what should happen when a tender other than the original is chosen?

How does the POS know a card is expired or closed (card data at refund time, or a decline from the card network), and is the switch to store credit automatic or does the cashier choose it? How are test sales seeded with MC_EXPIRED and AMEX_CLOSED, given they must have been valid at the time of sale?
For a split-tender refund, does the POS send one SAP message per tender or one message for the whole refund? If one, how are multiple tender types and amounts represented?
What are the exact formats and allowed values for tenderType (including store credit), amount and timestamp?

What starts the 5-minute clock (refund confirmation?), what is the retry interval, and must retries finish inside the 5 minutes? The test environment cannot delay a send, so how can a send at just under, exactly at, and just over 5 minutes be produced?
Does 'retries 3 times' mean 4 attempts in total (1 + 3 retries)? Is each attempt visible in the integration log? After the error log entry, is the message ever re-sent?
What must the error log entry contain (for example refundId, originalTxnId, failure reason, attempt count)?

coverage_notes: R2: the positive and negative cases are the boundary tests TC-003/TC-004 (allowed) and TC-005 (blocked).
R3: no standalone negative test. The only failure mode is refunding in the wrong order, which is already caught by the expected amounts in TC-007 (and TC-008, TC-010, TC-011).
R4: 'never exceed the original amount' is tested at the limit (TC-014) and just above it (TC-015, TC-016). It is not a fixed number in the BRD, so no separate just-below test was added.
R6: the negative case (valid card gets no store credit) is the 'No store credit issued' check in TC-001.

R7: the 5-minute boundary cannot be tested just below, at and just above with this test environment, because the SAP stub can fail sends but not delay them. TC-025 and TC-029 check the upper limit only; see Q-12.
Transaction IDs and SKUs (TXN-2xxx, SKU-1xx) are new sales to be seeded before execution; the BRD and test_env do not list existing sales.
All refunds are performed on 2026-11-01 at STR-0042, REG-03.
